_note: gd_study.json optimises the base alone and its result has no camera interface. This one puts the whole mount in the problem: the pedestal + the three female tabs are preserve, and the features cut into them (tab slots, M5 bore, nut pocket, thumb-screw knob clearance) are obstacles, so the optimiser can neither delete the mount nor fill its holes back in. The output STL is therefore a complete part, fixture included.

preserve._why: mount_only.stl is the real solid: pedestal + tabs with the features already cut. The pads are r=6 at radius 45 so they stay inside the r=52 disc. Re-exported 2026-08-04 with the widened case fits (slot 3.50 -> 3.80, bore 5.30 -> 5.60, knob pocket 22.0 -> 23.5), so this body is slightly smaller than the one the archived baseline result was solved on.

obstacle._why: mount_cuts.stl is exactly what tripod() subtracts, clipped to the height the part can reach. The clearance CANNOT eat the tabs: build_setup does `obstacle = obstacle & ~preserve`, so wherever the grown obstacle runs into mount_only.stl the preserve wins and the growth is discarded. The clearance only bites in the FREE design space -- which is exactly where it is needed, because that is where the optimiser was free to park material one voxel deep into the knob and nut pockets. 2.0 mm is a bit over one voxel at the 1.6 mm grid this study runs at.

_regions_why: loads and supports must be subsets of preserve. The 30 N hand push at the camera top reaches the hinge as 30 N shear plus Mx 1950 N*mm; the shear goes on the centre tab at the bolt axis and the moment as a couple on the pedestal top over its measured lever.

cases.name: LC1f  push 30 N from the front at the camera top
LC1b  push 30 N from the back at the camera top
LC2   crush 150 N down on the mount
LC3x  prise 150 N on one foot, the other two clamped
